dedupe_keys.name: economic census petroleum bulk stations and terminals storage capacity by facility product and station type

description: These Economic Census subject tables of the U.S. Census Bureau describe the petroleum bulk storage held by wholesale petroleum bulk stations and terminals, a part of the fuel supply chain that few open datasets quantify. Four tables are published for the 2012 and 2017 censuses in the Census Data API: petroleum bulk storage capacity by type of facility and type of product, by type of product and storage capacity size, by type of station and type of product, and the primary method of receiving petroleum bulk liquid products (for example pipeline, tanker or barge, rail or truck). Coverage: the United States and, for some tables, states; census years 2012 and 2017, with the 2022 census released on a flow basis. Access: the Census Data API datasets ecnpetrfac, ecnpetrprod, ecnpetrstat and ecnpetrrec (free key required) and the Economic Census tables on data.census.gov; free and public domain. Caveats: aggregate capacity only, with no facility locations or names; values are suppressed where they would disclose a business, and only wholesale bulk stations and terminals are covered, not refineries or retail stations. Simulation uses: sizing regional fuel storage buffers and receiving modes in fuel supply and outage models, for example how long terminals could supply a region after a pipeline or port disruption, and calibrating fuel logistics networks. Related records: the Economic Census record for the rest of the census, EIA petroleum supply statistics and refinery capacity reports, and the Commodity Flow Survey for fuel shipments.
